classes/abomination.title: Abomination
classes/abomination.content:
1. Investigate the Unnatural
Gain an extra 30% to your unnatural stat.
2. Unnatural Developments I
Choose one of the following to add. Note that this can allow you to go over your max in any of the base stats.





















Development NameDescriptionExtra Muscles+ 20% to Strength- 10% to CharismaExtra Appendages+ 20% to Dexterity-10% to ConstitutionPermanent Scars+ 20% to Constitution- 10% to Intellgence
3. Delve into madness
As a bonus home scene you can now do the “staying on the case” action, in addition to a normal home scene.
4. Unnatural Developments II
Choose one of the following to add. Note that this can allow you to go over your max in any of the base stats.





















Development NameDescriptionExaggerated TraitsGain several retractable claws, horns, or spurs. Your unarmed melee is now deals 1d12 of damage. Melee sneak attacks are at +20% as well.Stretchable AppendagesYour Limbs can how stretch unnaturally long. On a successful Dexterity check, you can stretch your limbs up to 30ft long. Note that this can be used to grab weapons out of an opponents hands.Accelerated RegenerationYour body heals broken bones, cuts and scrapes impossibly fast. Regen 2hp per turn during combat.
5. Numb mind
Gain an +30% bonus when rolling sanity.
6. Unnatural Developments III
Choose one of the following to add.





















Development NameDescriptionBoiling Blood-20% to Charisma.Touching your characters bare skin feels like acid. Any creature touching your skin takes 1d10 of damage per turn that they touch your skin.Tripartite brain- 20% to IntelligenceOn any roll below a 20% perform an additional action that turn.Dermal Armour-20% to DexterityGain an extra layer of Armour on your persons. Add an natural 3 Armour to your sheet. This Armour is not affected by durability.

classes/close-combat-specialist.title: Close combat specialist
classes/close-combat-specialist.content:
A Delta green specialist focusing mostly on melee abilities.
1  Mean right hook
Unarmed combat rolls and melee weapons can be replaced by strength rolls.
2. Stat Buff
+10% to any base stat. Example Strength, Constitution, Dexterity…
3. Killer Instincts

Killing monsters results in a 1d6 sanity gain
Monsters surviving a fight with your charicter results in a 1d6 sanity loss.

4. Tough it out
Once per session, when taking damage greater than a d4, reduce that damage to a d4
5. Lethal blow
On a successful critical strike, roll again.
6. Adrenaline Burst
Once per session, upon being downed, you character can get back up for two turns, during which they can attack, run, or do any action they please. Once those turns are expended, they will go down again.

80% Firearms

+10% to any base stat. Example Strength, Constitution, Dexterity…

Killing monsters results in a 1d6 sanity gain
Monsters surviving a fight with your charicter results in a 1d6 sanity loss.

classes/prepper.title: Prepper
classes/prepper.content:
1. Tinker
Demolitions, and Heavy Weapons rolls can be replaced with INT rolls
2. Stat Buff
+10% to any base stat. Example Strength, Constitution, Dexterity…
3. Inside buyers
Weapons purchases are processed at one level cheaper.
Ex: Unusual → Standard
4. Ghost Guns
Military Restricted weapons are no longer restricted and can be manufactured at home.
5. My baby
Creation of a custom weapon, Major Expense or below. This has the following buffs.

30% more accurate
or
1d6 more damaging

Upgrade your custom weapon once again.

Add 10% lethality to the weapon.
or
Add a 1d6 per turn (poison, fire, or radiation) effect.
or
A once per session detonator which destroys your weapon (You can spend a home scene to make a new one). Dealing 2d20 to anyone in a 30m radius.

classes/slick-talker.title: Slick Talker
classes/slick-talker.content:
1. Quick Talking
Replace Psychotherapy and Criminology with charisma rolls.
2. Stat Buff
+10% to any base stat. Example Strength, Constitution, Dexterity…
3. Mogging
Cause a distraction or do something out of ordinary to stun another creature. Roll contested Charisma against the target creatures Intelligence. On a success that creature receives a -30% debuff to it’s next action. On a critical success double this debuff.
Note: Players are REQUIRED to make a face at the DM while performing this action.
4. Quick Sew
When rolling first aid, roll two dice for the medical effect, and keep the higher one.
AND
Ignore the bleed out penalty when rolling first aid on a teammate.
5. Stat Buff II
+15% to any base stat. Example Strength, Constitution, Dexterity…
6. The Magnum
Player can now perform the action from level 3 (Mogging) while doing another action. Note this is a bonus action.

core-rules/combat.title: Combat
core-rules/combat.content:
Turns
Agents and Monsters both take turns during combat. Unless otherwise stated a agent or monster has one action per turn. A turn is about 8 seconds.
Initiative
The person who rolls first is determined by a combination of alertness and dexterity.
Being ambushed
If Agents is being ambushed or attacked, they must roll alertness, if they get a chance to use an action before they are attacked.
Dexterity
To determine the rolling order, agents will roll against their dexterity. The order is determined by how much you pass your dexterity roll by. Creatures or agent who fail dexterity skip their first turn, and take their actions at the start of the next turn.
Guns
Aimed Shots
If agents are using a gun, they can sacrifice an action to take the “aim” action. Taking the aim action skips their turn, but means their next firearms roll is at a +25% advantage.
Specific Shots
Agents can take a -40% penalty to their firearms skill to aim for a small specific part of the thing they are aiming at. This doubles the damage of their shot.
Cars
Car Crash
Car crashes happen in tiers. Each tier depends on how fast you are traveling, and what you are hitting. DM’s can decide what tier a car crash is. Generally speaking, if a player critical fails a drive roll, that is usually a medium car crash.





































TypeSpeed RangeScenariosVehicle StatusSaving RollDamageMinor Accidentbelow 15 mphBumping another car. Parking lot accident. Hitting a deer.Car operational.Constitution0 Damage on a pass.1d4 on a fail.Average Accident15 mpg - 40mphCrashing the car into a building. T-boning at an intersection going 30mph.Car requires engineering roll to fix.Constitution1d4 on a pass.1d8 on a fail.Major Accident+ 40mphHead on collision. Highway speed accident.Car destroyedConstitution1d8 on a pass.1d12 on a fail.
Ramming things with cars
Ramming things with a car is essentially a controlled car crash. It is highly dependent on how heavy the object is that you are hitting. When you ram something with a car, it deals double car crash damage to the thing being rammed, and standard car crash damage to the driver.

Example:
Agent Pine attempts to run over the deamon in the parking lot. Agent Pine is going about 30mph. Agent Pine passes his drive roll. Agent Pine fails his constitution roll, taking 1d8 damage. The deamon fails it’s constitution roll taking 1d8 damage.

Note: If two cars try to ram each other at the same time, both drivers take double damage.
Going down
If an agents HP is reduced to zero, they enter a downed state. They cannot move, and are bleeding out. The agent requires medical attention soon. The difficulty required to revive them will increase over time until they die. A successful first aid roll will revive them.





































Turns without medical AidOffset1+10% (Slightly Easier)20% (Normal)3-10% (Slightly Harder)4-30% (Difficult)5-50% (Very Hard)6-70% (Nearly Impossible)7Agent dies
Critical Hits
Critical hits result in an attack doing double damage.

core-rules/core-stats.title: Core Stats
core-rules/core-stats.content: Stat NameDescriptionStrengthA creatures brute strength. This is general measure of how much raw pounds per square inch a creature can output.Example: “I would like to smash that door down.”ConstitutionA general measure of how tough or durable a creature is. Note that player health is determined by how high their Constitution is.Example: “Your mouth tastes like copper. Roll Constitution. “DexterityA general measure of how fast or responsive a creature is when compared to other creatures.Example: “I would like to shoot that terrorist before he shoots me.”IntelligenceA general measure of how prepared a character is. This is also a measure of how well a creature can remember things.1. Remembering a Cheap Item: Players can roll Intelligence to “remember” to bring a cheap item(under 50$). Example: “Roll Intelligence to see if you have a flashlight.”2. Asking the DM a question: Players can also use Intelligence to ask the DM a basic or relatively common question.Example: “Would I get hurt jumping out of this moving car?”PowerGenerally speaking, this denotes the amount of determination a character has. Note that player starting sanity and breaking point is determined by how high their Power is.Example: “You can hear the voice of Shog-meail in your ear. Roll to resist the urge to lick the ancient totem.”CharismaA general measure of how good a creature is at interacting with humans, and socializing. This can be used in several ways, but below are the most common.1. Convincing others: Players can use this to convince other humans to do things for them.Example: “I would like to convince the bystander to leave.”2.  Determining Emotions: Players can use charisma to gain insight into how another human might be feeling.  Example: “Is she lying?”

core-rules/home-scenes.title: Home Scenes
core-rules/home-scenes.content:
Throughout the day, the normal adult tends to have this thing called “free time”. Typically they spend this time doing fun or relaxing things. Not you. As a secret agent you spend this time preparing for the next mission.

Stay on the case: Your agent remains on the case, researching unknown objects they have collected at the expense of their own sanity. This requires a Intelligence roll.
Learn a new Skill: Increase one of your detailed stats. roll Intelligence, on a success Add 1d10 on a failure add 1d6.
Restore Sanity: Conduct some sort of sanity regaining activity. Roll Sanity, on success gain 1d10, on failure gain 1d4 sanity.
Purchase Items: Your Character purchases things, and items.

List of Things to buy



Characters also level up every other mission.

core-rules/introduction.title: Introduction
core-rules/introduction.content:
Welcome to Redline
Who are your Agents?
Agents are players. These are people who have been brought into Redline, usually at the recommendation of a friendly supervisor. Your Agents agreed to be a part of the Redline organization, and are now on the hook 24/7 for protecting the world against unnatural threats. Agents are not paid per say, but if they make it to retirement, the agents will be rewarded with a large lump sum of money, tucked away in an investment account for them.
Overtime this exposure to the unnatural world will eat away at agent’s Sanity, and sometimes even augment their bodes. Agents will loose or gain (mostly lose) sanity by their actions in game. This sanity loss will overtime manifest as mental disorders, altering character behavior and abilities.
Agents come from a variety of backgrounds and specialties. [MORE HERE]


                  
                    Classes
                  
                


Gunslinger
Prepper
Close combat specialist
Slick Talker
Abomination



The handler and Missions
The handler (The DM), is a physical character who delegates missions to the players. This person can be whoever you want them to be. This handler is backed by the government, and has access to all police records, government security cameras, and other discrete methods of gathering information. They can bail your Agents out of trouble, call them, and provide forged documents.
There is however, one stipulation. If the handler is killed or otherwise incapacitated, the campaign ends. No more missions. All Agents return to being normal citizens or are killed. Due to this reason, handlers usually live in seclusion, and leave the Combat and the risky dice rolls to the agents.


                  
                    Home life options
                  
                

Throughout the day, the normal adult tends to have this thing called “free time”. Typically they spend this time doing fun or relaxing things. Not you. As a secret agent you spend this time preparing for the next mission.

Stay on the case: Your agent remains on the case, researching unknown objects they have collected at the expense of their own sanity.
Learn a new Skill: Increase your skill in an area, roll INT, on a success Add 1d10 on a failure add 1d6.
Restore Sanity: Conduct some sort of sanity regaining activity. Roll Sanity, on success gain 1d10, on failure gain 1d4 sanity.
Purchase Items: Agent purchases Items & Gear

core-rules/items--and--gear.title: Items & Gear
core-rules/items--and--gear.content:
Buying things.
Buying things requires good finances. Upon buying things, Agents are required to make a finance roll.
Purchasing items is done though a finance roll. If players desire to increase their finance, they can purchase an investment, or they can level up their finance skills. If an item is not below on the items and gear list, DM’s can make the items stats whatever they deem fair, and the cost difficulty should reflect the approximant real world value.

Critical Success on finance:
Player get the object they were looking for easily, and at a lower price than expected. The player also acquires a free “short term investment” item.


Success on finance:
Player purchases item.


Failure on finance:
Player is unable to purchase the item.


Critical Failure on finance:
Player makes a major financial or logical burden. They do not get the item. What happens here is up to the DM’s discretion.

free-missions/0.-introduction.title: 0. Introduction
free-missions/0.-introduction.content:
Handler Eyes Only! 
                  
                

Players turn back now! Do not spoil any of the missions!


Below is a series of free missions. You can play them in any order, but the recommended order is likely best. This follows a Redline group based on the pacific northwest.
Introduction and Background
Each player was working as a normal, government worker, until one day their supervisor asked them if they want to be a part of something bigger. Not a public role like a police officer, but a  secretive role for a mysterious organization. All of you agents accepted this offer. Each agent was given a cheap flip phone, and told to wait for a call.
Missions


                  
                   1. Walk in the Park
                  
                

easy 3-4hrs
Agents investigate a mission child case from 45 years ago.




                  
                   2. Cottons Catastrophe
                  
                

easy 3-4hrs
Another Redline team needs backup.




                  
                   3. The Bird Mission
                  
                

medium 2-3hrs
Agents investigate a bizarre murder.




                  
                   4. Red Alert
                  
                

hard 2-3hrs
A simple, easy mission to relax on.




                  
                   5. Doomscrolling
                  
                

hard 2-3hrs
Agents track down a suspected wizard for shrimpifying people




                  
                   6. Sketchway
                  
                

hard 3-4hrs
Agents run to the local cornerstore to get some medicine


Redline is a volunteer project. More missions are planned and in the works.

free-missions/1.-walk-in-the-park.title: 1. Walk in the Park
free-missions/1.-walk-in-the-park.content:

Hook
Park Rangers at Olympia national park recently found a lost child. Face id’s match them to a missing child case… from 45 years ago. The park rangers and the child are currently at a ranger station on the edge of the national park. The time is currently 4pm. The players will be given fake FBI badges under the guise that they are investigating the missing child case.
Objectives
Retrieve the child. Cover up the circumstances surrounding their appearance.
Entering the park
As the Players start driving to the park rain starts coming down hard. Players that are driving must make a DRIVE check. There is no cell signal while in the park, only landlines function.

Drive Check: If the driver passes a drive check the players arrive before sundown. If the driver fails the drive check the players arrive after sundown. If the driver critical fails, the players crash their car. Combat > Car Crash
pass - > Get there on time
fail - > Roads are slippery. Players arrive 2 hrs late.
critical fail -> Car Crash

The Ranger Station
The rangers station is a somewhat new wooden building with a metal roof. The building has several glass windows, which are currently closed. There is a gravel parking lot, which could seat up to ~40 cars. This parking lot contains only three vehicles, a Subaru, and two park ranger trucks.

There are four people within the Ranger station. Note that either ranger can give you a map of the area.
Ranger Rick
Talks with a stutter. He is a 6ft thin  young adult male. He originally found John wandering in the forest near the old fire watch while doing routine patrols on the park trails. He says “That place always smells weird”.

Successful Charisma roll at +40% to convince him that you are FBI agents.
Stats


Firearms : 60% (1d10) Glock 22
Melee : 50%
Drive : 60%
Law : 30%
First Aid : 40%
All Core Stats : 50%
All other Stats : 5%

The Child (John Williams)
A small boy, appears to be about 11 years old. He has wet hair and is wearing a Hoodie that says “I Love Olympia National Park”. He also has a very large national forest service baseball cap on this head, with the tag still on it.
He is crying constantly, without saying anything. He will curl up into a ball and refuse to be moved if agents try to move him. He has very very little memory, he doesn’t remember who his parents are, or how he got here.

Searching John
A successful search or forensics roll will reveal that he has a strange circular scar on the back of his neck.


Calming John Down
On a successful Psychotherapy roll He calms down, and will listen to player instructions, even during combat.


Successful First Aid Roll (Tending to John)
He had a scrape on his knee, but it already has been treated.

Ranger Samantha
A middle aged woman park ranger. She is trying to calm John down, and failing miserably. She will ask the agents if they have located johns parents.
Stats

Firearms : 60% (1d10) Glock 22
Melee : 50%
Drive : 60%
Law : 30%
First Aid : 40%
All Core Stats : 50%
All other Stats : 5%

Elderly Hiker Couple
A pair of elderly hikers. They are sheltering from the rain, they will run away if confronted with combat.
A little after the agents arrive
A little bit after the agents arrive, one Shog`a-lite will arrive. These creatures will observe from a distance at first (Successful alertness for anyone standing outside to notice this. )
Once they are done observing, they will attempt (And succeed) at mind controlling ranger rick. Ranger Rick will begin to act mechanical, loose his stutter, and attempt to drag the child outside by any means necessary. If the agents intervene, he will try to shoot them. Ranger Samantha will side with ranger Rick in any conflict, regardless of if she is mind controlled.
The Old Fire Watch

An old rickety fire watch, there is a well worn path from the ranger station to the fire watch.

Searching the station
A successful search roll will reveal there is a well worn path around the station, you can see a thick layer of dust inside the actual station. No ones been inside for a very long time.


Looking for clues on how John got here
A successful forensics roll reveals that there small patch of blood, as well as a small divot in the muddy ground. This is likely where Ranger Rick found John.

Hiking there
Walking to the fire watch should take about 15 minutes uphill. The rain is heavy, and the wind is loud. Players can hear the trees cracking and whistling as they walk there.
Two Shog`a-lites will ambush the players as they return to the ranger station from the fire watch. A successful alertness check to notice them before they assault the players.

Inside the Fire Watch
The inside of the fire watch is damp, and smells vaguely of mold. There is a small marmot living in the fire watch tower, which has Taken residence in the fire watch. There is also some file cabinets with various stacks of papers.

Searching inside the fire watch
There is a small box on the floor with a single grenade inside of it. Note, throwing this grenade requires a dexterity check.


Searching in the fire watch
A successful Bureaucracy roll reveals this fire watch used to be a cover for the Redline organisation. They were using this fire watch to “keep watch” on some nearby fungal growths. Gain 1d6 in unnatural skill.

Resolutions
Assuming the Players kill all of the Shog`a-lites and retrieve John, they can simply return to The Handler. He will hand John off to an unnamed female agent with blonde hair (This is Agent Cotton, but if you haven’t done Cottons Catastrophe don’t introduce her).

Hook
All of the agents receive a call at 1am at night. Anther group of agents is in trouble. They need backup and fast.
The group of agents in trouble was last reported investigating a reported death cult at a temp worker agency located in Moses Lake, Washington. The fine details of the investigation are classified.
If you’ve never been to Moses lake, don’t go. The town it self is comprised of trailer parks, golf courses, and crumbing administrative buildings. The other group of agents were last seen entering and investigating Wellborn temp agency. That was 6 hours ago.
Objectives
Recover the briefcase. Recover Agent Cotton. Do not open the briefcase, it contains the ultimate  weapon.
The story
Outside of the building
The building looks like a visibly aged brick office building. It has two stories, and several thick windows on the sides which have been barred and have the blinds drawn.
The glass front door is locked, and the lights are off. Peering inside the building agents cannot see anything out of the ordinary. There is a reception desk at the front with a PC stationed at the front.
If the Agents decide to circle the building they will find a small window which peers into a break room. They can make out a few chairs, and old mirowave, and a fridge, as well as some coffee stains on the carpeted floor.

Entering the building
The front door is locked. It uses a key card reader to authenitcate people coming into the building. Players do not have a key card.

Hacking the keycard reader
Using either a criminology roll or a computer science roll players can unlock the door via RIFD spoofing the keycard.


Smashing the door
A successful strength check will result in the door being smashed in, allowing players to walk into the building. This however has the risk of drawing in the police to the building. The Scenario starts at 1am. If players smash the door this roll a luck roll every 3 hours to see if a police offiecer notices the smahed door.


Entering through the break room window
A successful criminology or strength check to either unlock or smash the window. This window is facing the alleyway and it not visable to the public.

The lone survivor
Agent Cotton is the lone survivor of the “boiling donut” cell. Is had two other members who are dead in the basement. Agent Cotton is inside the basement trying to move one of the bodies outside of the basement so she can dispose of her teammates corpse. If the players make too much noise, roll alertness for Agent Cotton to see if she detects them.

Hearing Agent Cotton
If agents pass an alterness check they get to hear the sounds of Agent Cotton dragging a body up the stairs.

Tinfoil
Agent Cotton is wearing a tinfoil hat. She has a briefcase in her left hand, and a UZI in her right hand. There is blood all down her trenchcoat and pant leg. She has bullet holes in her trenchcoat.
Agent Cotton is jumpy, and will not trust the agents at first. She is not expecting backup, and will aim her gun at them if provoked or supervised. She will try to verify the agents identity by calling the handler. She will refuse to let go of the briefcase unless a player convinces her with a critical success on charisma.
Upon verifying the authenticity of the agents she will desperately try to convince them to wear tinfoil. She does not have any more tinfoil left, other than the hat she is currently wearing.

Locating tinfoil
Passing a search roll reveals tinfoil in the break room. Agents can also roll intelligence to have brought tinfoil.

Searching the offices / Managers office
There are mounds of paper inside of the managers office. The other offices are more tidy, but it’s still very very messy and a little moldy.

Hacking a computer: On a successful computer science roll, you can determine that this temp agency was bringing a large number of applicants in for interviews, and then those people are not being referred to jobs, instead just marked  in the system as “feed”.


Searching file cabinets and paper stacks: On a successful bureaucracy roll you find that this temp agency has created zero jobs in the past 2 years.

The basement
The basement smells like gunpowder and copper. There is a short landing, and then spiraling staircases that go down. There is a body shoved up against the right wall. It is a middle aged balding white male. He has a Glock-17 in is right hand. His chest has been crushed.

Investigating the cause of death
Forensics roll. If pass he was killed Blunt force trauma. He was killed instantly.

Agent Cotton will tell you that this was previously Agent John. She says Agent Salmon is lower down in the stairs… resting.


Looking down the center
There is no bottom. Roll sanity, on pass take 1d6 damage. On fail take 1 damage.

An Intrusion
After the player have been inside the building for 15 or so minutes, a Shog`a-wrath will teleport inside of the building. He is heavily damaged, part of a samari sword is lodged in his thigh, and there are three bullet imprints on his back. He will try to crush any players within his reach. DM’s can flip a coin to see if he teleports to the basement or the main building.
Opening the briefcase
Players may try to open the briefcase. Inside is a rubber duck kitchen timer. It has a maximum of 5 minutes and a minimum of 1 minutes on it’s time. If activated it will make a clicking noise.

If the timer goes off: If the timer goes off, the rubber duck will clone itself, with each clone making a clone of itself every millisecond for 20 seconds. It will due this until there is a maximum of 2^{38} total ducks nearby. This will level building and the nearby town, rushing them in rubber ducks. Anyone standing next to this when it activates takes 1d100 of damage.

The Interview
Around 5am a nervous high school student in wrinkly flannel and khakis will arrive. They are here for a job interview with the supposed temp agency. They will leave if harasses, and then will enter if the door is open.

free-missions/3.-the-bird-mission.title: 3. The Bird Mission
free-missions/3.-the-bird-mission.content:

Hook
The Agents are called to meet at Sea-Tac airport. Airport Security flags each agent and pulls them aside into a small conference room. Inside the conference room is the handler.
A delta green friendly, Dr. Parsons was killed yesterday in his laboratory at the University of Oregon. His research was primarily into birds. The handler takes out a thumbdrive and plugs it into a nearby TV screen. He then plays a CCTV footage video. The video is as described below.

Scene opens. The camera is aimed at a large tree in the center of an open courtyard. Various crows and other birds are nesting and squawking inside of the tree.
A tall, pale, elderly male sprints into the courtyard, holding sort sort of vial in his hands. All of the crows go silent.
The crows descend upon the man, ripping at his eyes and other body parts until he collapses.

The Handler will then access a nearby printer to print out fake school ID’s for the agents. Each agent is traveling under the guise of being a visiting professor from another university. Agents may decide what their fake PhD is in, and their fake professor name.
Objectives
Travel to the OSU aviary. Determine Cause of death. Prevent cause of death from happening again.
The campus
The oregon state campus is huge, and people are walking around. The sun is shining, and some birds watch you from the trees.

Open carrying weapons:
If the agents are open carrying weapons this cause the local campus security to intercept them. Oregon state university has a policy against bringing weapons onto campus, and they will try to get the players to leave.

The Aviary
The aviary is a large open canopy building, with large greenhouse glass windows, and a open roof. The aviary also doubles as a botanical garden. Birds squawk and chirp from above. There is a large tree in the center of the aviary.
Off to the side, marked by yellow police tape is a red stain on the floor. Nearby is a black body bag. It contains Dr Parsons.

Forensic investigation
A successful forensics or search will tell the agents that he died of the birds killing him. Agents also find some broken glass, and a fait smell of gasoline on his coat.
He also has the keys to his office in his coat pocket.

The birds
Squawking. Pooping. Squawking and pooping. The birds are flying around the agents, mostly paying them little mind. There is a small bird bath in the corner that some of them are splashing in.

Are the birds acting normally?
A successful roll for Science or Unnatural will tell the agents that the birds appear normal. For now.


The Tree
There is a large oak tree towards the side of the aviary, which has many crows, and crow nests in the tree. The agents can feel them watching. There are about ~100-200 crows inside the aviary flying in and out of the aviary.

Shiny?
If the agents pass an alertness check or a search check of the surrounding area, they will notice a shiny object near a landing in the middle of the tree.

The top of the tree
At the top of the tree is a small setup, where a batch of mushrooms is growing. Several cameras have been set up to watch the mushrooms. Agents will need to make a strength check to climb up the tree.
If agents reach the top of the tree, each bird will fall silent slowly. As the agents crest the top of the tree near the landing, the birds will stop moving, and making noises, all watching the agent.

Destroying the mushrooms:
Destroying the mushrooms will cause the bird swarm to fall out of the sky, with all of them collapsing on the ground dead.


Firing a weapon:
Any loud noise such as a gunshot this will trigger a police response, and likely a swat team response. Players will have 1d4 turns of notice in the form of police sirens to escape before they get swatted. The handler will be unable to prevent this kind of police response.

The truth
The mushroom entity at the top of the tree has formed a hivemind with the rest of the nearby birds. If it thinks that agents are a threat for any reason it will form a Swarm of Birds, and attack the players.
Dr Parsons Office
His office is a mess, and there is a cold cup of coffee, that has been sitting there for some time. As you walk by, you can hear some students whispering about how he died after being F*cked by a crow.

Searching the office
With a successful search or bureaucracy roll, the agents can find a small locked locker near the side of the room, in which he has

Shotgun (birdshot)
Also detailed images of the fungal growth on the top of the tree, with size measurements, and other related things.
Flash drive, containing research on the fungal growth in the tree, with a draft of a paper called “hallucinogenic fungal interactions in avians”.
Fungal headphone contraption_ Small strange headphones with a glass cap around each ear, with some sort of fungus in the ear caps.
These allow for you to “hear” animals. However they require a luck roll, otherwise you hear gibberish.

free-missions/4.-red-alert.title: 4. Red Alert
free-missions/4.-red-alert.content:

Hook
The Handler calls the players to a popular burger joint late at night. Normally he meets them in his retrofitted RV. As the agents arrive at the burger joint, they notice that the parking lot is empty except for a U-Haul, and another man in a dark tinted car, whom is playing on his phone.
After sitting the players down, he admits the last couple of missions were a bit hectic, and he’s hoping to give the players a safer, more simple mission for today. The handler will pay for whatever food the agents want.
The original mission
The goal is to transport a box in a U-Haul from the parking lot to a self-storage container outside of city limits. Easy. The handler does not mention the contents of the box.
An Interruption
The Handler then finishes his burger and takes the agents out to the parking lot to show them the U-Haul. Just as he steps out of the door a gunshot rings out. A small red dot appears on the handlers chest and he collapses. The handler screams in pain. The handler has been shot.
Current Objective
“Get that son of a b!tch! and get me to a god damn hospital!”
The Man with the Gun
A man wearing a black hoodie and a ski mask is sitting in the drivers eat of a dodge charger. He is holding a russian SVD. If any of the players are in sight, he’ll try to take a quick parting shot that them, and then attempt to drive away. He is the same person that the agents saw waiting in the parking lot.
Stats:
HP: 16

Firearms : 60%  --- 1d12 (SVD)
Drive    : 50%
Computer science : 80%
All other stats 50%


Giving Chase:
Giving chase is difficult, but the characters could pursue him in the U-Haul or a personal car. This will create a car chase. This means the driver of each car must contest their drive rolls. If the players fail three drive rolls in a row, the loose the assassin. If either driver critical fails, they crash their car.



Crashing:
Each agent rolls intelligence to see if they remembered their seatbelt in the event of a crash. If succeed, take 1d8 damage, if fail, agents take 1d12. The assassin remembered his seatbelt, and will take only 1d8 damage if crashing.
If the assassin survives the crash he will attempt to kill the agents pursuing with his gun.


Capturing:
If agents manage to capture the assassin, he will scream conspiring nonsense, about how the government is mind controlling birds, and how capitalism is controlled by a hidden wizard cult. He will not reveal how he tracked the handler down unless you interrogate it out of him.


Interrogating
On a successful charisma roll, he’ll reveal that he had been tracking the handler and “his blonde deamon”, through a hacked backdoor on the public traffic cameras.

The handler
The Handler is bleeding out, very fast. He will die unless given immediate medical attention or taken to a hospital. Please note, if the handler dies, the game ends.

How is he feeling?
The handler has been reduced to 8/16 hp. He is bleeding out at -1hp per turn. If someone passes a medical check on him, he will stabilize, and stop bleeding out.


If stabilized:
If you stabilized the handler he will attempt to make a call on his cell phone, he will then give to the GPS co-ordantes to the Handlers RV, where he will meet a waiting Agent Cotton, who will patch him up, if possible.

Meeting with agent cotton
If the agents get away they will meet a bleary eyed, very sleep deprived Agent Cotton. She has parked the handlers RV in the middle of the woods. She will escort the handler to the RV, where she will operate surgery on him. Agents are permitted inside the RV.
Completing the delivery
If the agents secure the handler, and capture / kill the would be assassin, they may desire to complete the delivery assigned to them. This part of the mission is entirely optional.

The self storage locker:
The keys to the U-Haul are in the front seat. There is also a key to a self storage locket outside of city limits.


The rattling box in the back:
The back of the truck contains a Angel of Desire trapped in a nailed shut wooden box. This box will rattle and shake every time the agents walk near it.

free-missions/5.-doomscrolling.title: 5. Doomscrolling
free-missions/5.-doomscrolling.content:

Hook
The handler calls the team to his RV at 9pm at night on a friday. They have located a wizard who is suspected of turning people and small dogs into shrimp. Through sheer luck, we managed to get a copy of his bus ticket out of town.
Objectives
A suspected Wizard will board a Metro Bus(east bound Division 25 stop 3 @ 1:23 am). Bring him in alive or dead. Make sure to bring in any items he has on his persons.
The Bus
The bus will arrive around 1:23am. It is cold and gloomy, the only light around them is from streetlights.
People on the bus
As the players get on the bus you can see there are two total people on the bus… Well, three if you count the bus driver.
The Grumpy Elderly Man
A grumpy elderly man, will snarl at anyone nearby.  He is nearly black out drunk, and reeks of alcohol.  He is spread out, taking up two bus seats in the disabled section. You can see two bottles of beer under his left arm.
Stats
HP : 12

Revolver (60% firearms) 1d8
Unarmed (40%)
All other stats (30%)

The bird lover
A young white male. His is watching some kind of anime on his phone, with the phone speaker on full blast. He is also wearing a red angry birds hat. If engaged in conversation he will adamantly talk about his favorite game, which is about slingshotting birds into houses constructed about pigs. (I can’t say what game due to copyright)
Stats
HP : 10

Unarmed (40%)
All other stats (30%)

The Bus Driver
The bus driver is not paying attention, and is looking down and is scrolling on his phone. He does not acknowledge the players as they get on the bus. He is wearing a bus drivers uniform, and is middled aged and balding.
Stats
HP : 16

Unarmed (40%)
Unnatural (80%)
All other stats (30%)

His Phone
His phone is a pure obsidian box. It is not turned on, and it is the thing controlling the bus. On a successful unnatural roll, a player can use it to transport themselves and the bus to any dimension or place. On a successful (INT - 20%) roll, the players can go to the previous dimension or next dimension.
Special Abilities
If prompted he will cast spells to defend himself.

Shrimpify:
On a successful unnatural roll, he will turn the effected creature or item into a small dog sized shrimp. Note that this is extremely painful. This transformation only lasts for 1 minute. If an agent is threating him, he will turn them or their weapons into shrimp.

Uh oh, where are we now?
After about 3-10 minutes (this can be decided by a dice roll or DM discretion) the bus will teleport to a new plane of existence / Location. This will continue until the players apprehend the bus driver or his phone.
The bus will go to the following dimensions in order. Swiping up on the phone will bring you down one dimension, and up will bring you down one dimension. Swiping down while in the endless beach will being you to Spokane, and swiping up while in the shopping mall will also bring you back to Spokane.
On each location change

Roll Sanity ( 1d6 fail … loose 1 on success)

1. The Endless Beach
Sunlight fills the bus windows. The bus doors open and briny sand sloshes into the bus. The sky is grey, yellow sand, and small briny pools of water stretch for as long as you can see. There’s a semi-dense fog blocking the long distance view.

Searching or looking outside
You can see tall (2 story) things walking around in the fog. Its hard to make out what they are.


Getting left behind
In the event that a player is left behind in his location, one of the tall creatures will come over to interact with them.


Tall Fella
A tall 2 story man made of twisted rebar and road signs. They speak all languages, but only talk in a customer service like voice. It always refers to you as “valued customer”.
Stats
HP : 50


Charisma (40%)
Unnatural (80%)
All other stats (30%)



First Offer : Send you back to where you came, in exchange for all of your hair, and 30% of your toes.
Second Offer : Send you back to where you came, in exchange for all of your hair, and a foot.
Third Offer : Send you back to where you came, in exchange for all of your hair, a foot, and 10% of your grey matter.
If the player haggles to much or tries to kill him repeatedly, he will simply attack with a bite (75% 1d20), until they die.

2. Falling forever
Nothing, just inky blackness outside of the bus, every single player gets the impression of falling.

Getting off the bus
If a player gets off the bus without a tether, they will gently float away. Them and the bus are “falling” at the same speed. Have the player roll either INT of SAN to force themselves to step outside.


Getting left behind
If an agent is left behind, they will fall contentiously in inky blackness until they starve to death.

3. Shrimp Town

“I made it take ya to shrimp town” - The bus driver says this out loud while giggling.
An reddish glow fills the bus, and you look outside to see … lots and lots of Human Sized Shrimp. There are small wooden huts around, as well as a campfire, where several human sized shrimp are roasting smaller, normal sized shrimp on a fire.
A shrimp shaped crescent moon can be seen in the sky, with smaller orange lights were the stars are.

Getting off the bus
The Human Sized Shrimp run away in terror.


Getting left behind
Without teleportation, there is no way to get home from this dimension. But hey… At least they have an endless supply of shrimp.

4. Shopping mall
Quiet pleasant music plays, you can’t identify what song it is, or what the words are. rows and rows of grocery isles full of toothpaste. stretch out in every direction. This is the cornerstone from 6. Sketchway .
The final stop on the bus, assuming the players do not stop the bus driver until then. The Bus driver will get off after this stop, and leave without saying anything.

Getting off the bus
1-2 Hungry Mannequins will attack the player in 1-6 minutes if the players linger here.


Getting left behind
If the bus driver somehow escapes the players and leaves them behind, the players will be trapped in the cornerstore from 6. Sketchway.

free-missions/6.-sketchway.content:

Hook
The Handler calls the team to the Handlers RV, and the handler instructs them that they need to escort Agent Cotton to the cornerstore to get her medication. He hands the players a brown leather wallet. Agent Cotton already knows where to go, and it wearing a hiking backpack.
Objectives
Acquire Agent Cotton’s medication.
Inside the leather wallet
There are three white milky coins, each has a smile etched into each one.

Identifying the coins:

Successful Unnatural Roll: They are a form of wizard currency.
Successful Forensics Roll: They are make of human bone. Roll sanity for 1d4.


The Store
The store is in the middle of the sketchy side of downtown Spokane. There are several homeless milling around the building. The cornerstone is clearly shutdown, and surrounded by razor wire fences. It has several graffiti tags on the side of the building. The door to the building is not locked.

Entering the building, the players will be greeted with several racks of vitamins. Agent Cotton knows which way to go by a small map on her phone. Her phone is on 3% battery.
The entrance that the players walked through on the real world connects to the larger “shopping dimension”. This creates a “bigger on the inside effect”. Upon realizing this any player must roll sanity, and take 1d4 san loss on success, and 1d10 sanity loss on failure.
The corner store is enormous, spanning over 200 total miles of shelves and items. Items on shelves do not decay, and do not perish.
Isles are given near nonsensical names such as “Vitamin D 56K”. Isle names are also given nonsensical names such as “Loafs of Loaf AX7”.
Items on the shelves
Items on the shelf span multiple different languages, however the pictures and advertisements on them seem to blur together. Expiration dates also given non-sense names such as “August -3 202A”.
Things in the mall
If the players make too much noise, or walk for more than 2 hours, roll luck. If under 60%, two Hungry Mannequins or Impersonator Mannequins are nearby. If given the chance, they will attempt to attack the players and eat their personal information.

Dave’s shop
Outside of the circular store, the isles and racks simply end, opening up to long near infinite stretches of open warehouse. There are no mannequins here. Players can see Dave’s shop in the distance from a long ways away. It appears to be a log cabin. There is a small drive through window in which Dave is standing.
The man himself
Wearing a wizard hat, cloak, and ski gloves. Dave is insane and erratic, his only goal is to make deals with the players.
The exchange
Upon receiving the 3 silver dollars, Dave will abruptly vanish, and then return 5-10 seconds later. His beard will look longer, and he will be wearing different clothes. He will hand Agent Cotton an unmarked brown paper bag. Dave and Agent Cotton have met before, he does not try to make any deals with her.
Bargaining
After buying the medicine, Dave will try to sell the players on exchanging their hair for various items. These can be any variation of nonsensical items, like for example “double phone, giraffe legs”.

Making a deal with Dave:
Dave will ask for percentages of the players “hair” in exchange for things. He says “I want hair”, but he is not thinking of human hair. He wants the players lungs.




















ItemCostExampleMinor magical item20% of your “hair”.Permanent reduction of that players consituion by 2d6.A phone with infinite bandwith.Medium magical item40% of you “hair”.Permanent reduction of the players constitution by 3d6.A bulletproof shirt.

monsters/angel-of-desire.content:
These are human-like statues, their body is frozen in place, however they can still do a sort of “gliding action.”
These “creatures” simply want to be as close to a human as possible. They will “glide” toward the closest person that they can see. The further away, the faster they will glide.
High Speeds
These statues will accelerate toward the nearest person, they accelerate at roughly the speed of a car, with an upper speed capacity of 900 MPH. This acceleration is uniform.

A Mannequin, these exist within the The Shopping Mall, these Mannequins often stand out from the others, settling down in the middle of a path, or leaning against a wall. They are pale white, and often have clothes from the wrong time period on them.
Their goal is to gain an identity, they will do this by eating the “personal information” of their victims.
What counts as personal info

ID’s
Tatoos
Hair
Wallets

monsters/impersonator-mannequin.content:
A Mannequin, these exist within the The Shopping Mall. They will pretend to be the person whose personal information they have stole, matching that person in appearance and voice.
They do not, however, replicate a persons memories, and know nothing about outside the mall. This can be used to “sniff” them out.
Reproduction
If this creature successfully “eats” another persons identity, they spawn a new Hungry Mannequin.
Stats
8hp

Attempt to steal object off person 60%

Chase (60%)

free-missions/npcs/the-handler.title: The Handler
